title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The Climate Resilient and Environmentally Sustainable Solutions Somalia/Somaliland (CRESS Somalia/Somaliland) programme will work in Banadir, Somalia and Somaliland. It aims to contribute to Concern Somalia’s Green Graduation and Climate Resilience thematic programmes, and the goal of the grant is to provide inclusive climate resilient and environmentally sustainable livelihood opportunities to vulnerable populations in Banadir. The programme will support over 160,290 people living in extreme poor households including those headed by women, households with disabled members and young people. This will be done through households receive asset/capital transfer to make investment in productive assets in diversified employment activities, households linked to formal financial services and barriers are addressed, environmental restoration and damage mitigation measures are in place and increased awareness on environmental protection and conservation.. OVERALL COUNTRY PROG: To provide inclusive climate resilient and environmentally sustainable livelihood opportunities to vulnerable populations in Banadir and Somaliland. SPECIFIC OUTCOME: RM ADaptation 2: Land and soil degradation is target location is significant and the environment has a low regenerative capacity. One of the main drivers of this is climate change, as it leads to prolonged droughts, erratic rainfall patterns, increased soil erosion, reduced vegetation cover, and more frequent extreme weather events. These funds will enable the Somaliland programme to expand activities aimed at restoring climate impacted natural resources. This will include watershed management through construction of soil bunds, gabion checks and planting edges to constructed watershed areas. Restoration of vegetation and promoting water harvesting techniques, such as, earth dams and underground water storage tanks. These activities reduce soil erosion, maintain existing forestry, support the land to retain water and reduce erosion and runoff, and increase vegetation cover and improving water retention from rainwater in target communities. This will address climate change driven vulnerabilities 1-4 above. These type of activities are mentioned in the OECD DAC Rio Markers for Climate Handbook within the Indicative Table to Guide Rio Marking by Sector/Sub-Sector this falls under Agriculture (CRS Code =311) and is under activity Sustainable climate-resilient farming methods which scores a Rio Marker score of 2 for adaptation. DRR 1: This outcome promotes imp[roved environmental restoration and managtement through a variety of activities that will enhance communities's resilience to future shocks.Aid to the environment 1: This outcome supports land rehabilitation through soil bund construction and gabion checks.Capacity Building 1: Ministry of Agriculture officials at district and regional levels will be involved in the selection of both lead and fellow farmers and co-facilitate the trainings, thereby increasing their capacity on the training components for lead farmers.Gender Equality 1: a gender lens is applied at every stage and a gender transformative approach is taken to tackle harmful gender norms, attitudes and practices.Nutrition 1: The promotion of rainwater harvesting (polythene sheets to collect rainwater) supports nutrition during the lean season.
